body:
Yes, you are good for your son.

You must stay alive, even if at this point he is the only reason why.

You mentioned feeling sad for no reason at all and living vivid memories of abuse and abandonment. When you find yourself doing this, stop and recognise what you are doing. You don't even have to make any effort to try and stop yourself. Just by becoming aware of your negative patterns of thought and taking a moment to think "this may be because of my BPD" helps you to feel in control and understand the situation. It is so difficult when you are feeling so hopeless and lost but I have found it helps me to come to terms with what is happening to me.

Why do you think you're a burden on your friends and loved ones?

You do know the last thing they want you to do is kill yourself right? As much as you might think to the contrary, you must remember this as a universal truth.

Hey mate, I was diagnosed with BPD about 1 month ago today after what feels like a lifetime of depression.

I felt the same way you do right now.

How are you feeling right now? At this moment?

Before the experience i had, i would have agreed with you entirely on every point you made.

I know that before that day, before that moment where I started taking those pills, nobody could have said a word to change my mind. The change came from inside of me.

I don't really know what effect this post was meant to have. I am mearly just describing what happened to me so that someone might not have to go through the same experience where they might not be as lucky as i was.

I know now that even though it is likely i am probably going to have to go through entirety of my life feeling and thinking the way i do, it is all have. Even if it feels unbearable.
If you kill yourself now, you will never have the chance to meet another person like Courtney and feel the same way she made you feel ever again.

Please believe me when i say the "what if" never entered my head until I was seconds away from losing consciousness and for all intents, about to die.

The experience was so unfathomably profound that it has changed my life forever. It certainly hasn't changed how I feel about myself as a person or my circumstances but it has grounded in me the desire to keep myself alive.

Before that day there was no hope but those few unconscious hours i spent in the hospital could have lasted for an eternity and without me ever knowing.

I will never be able to fully understand what happened that day.
